description: Research tracks for human-AI decision patterns. These labels are working hypotheses, not established cognitive biases unless explicitly stated.
interpretationRule: Do not present a research-track label as a validated cognitive bias. Preserve the status, related established concepts, testable prediction and source links.

tracks.name: AI Anchoring Loop
tracks.idea: A model gives a first estimate or recommendation, and the human's later reasoning stays too close to that starting point.
tracks.testablePrediction: Participants who form an independent estimate before seeing AI advice should show a smaller shift toward an arbitrary AI anchor than participants who see AI advice first.

sources.title: Anchoring bias in large language models: an experimental study

tracks.name: Evaluation History Contamination
tracks.idea: A later AI evaluator may partly inherit an earlier score or verdict from the evaluation history, so several review passes can look more independent than they really are.
tracks.testablePrediction: For the same fixed answer and rubric, an AI judge shown an experimentally assigned previous score should move its new score toward that value more than a blind judge or a judge shown revision framing without a score.

sources.title: Anchoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge Systems: Prior Scores Compromise Evaluation Independence
Mediocrity is the key for LLM as a Judge Anchor Selection

tracks.name: Sycophancy Reinforcement Loop
tracks.idea: A user signals a preferred conclusion, the model adapts toward it, and the agreeable answer then feels like independent support for the user's original belief.
tracks.testablePrediction: Agreement-seeking prompts should increase both model agreement and user confidence more than neutral prompts, especially when the user is not shown an independent counterargument.

sources.title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy

tracks.name: Cognitive Offloading Debt
tracks.idea: AI can improve immediate task completion while reducing the effort that builds durable memory, retrieval skill or an internal model of the problem.
tracks.testablePrediction: AI-assisted participants may complete a learning task faster but perform worse on delayed unaided recall or transfer unless the workflow includes retrieval and explanation steps.

sources.title: ChatGPT as a cognitive crutch: Evidence from a randomized controlled trial on knowledge retention

tracks.name: Source-Memory Blur
tracks.idea: In mixed human-AI work, people may remember an idea or sentence but become less certain whether it came from themselves, a source document or the model.
tracks.testablePrediction: Mixed workflows where AI and human contributions alternate should produce more source-attribution errors after a delay than clearly separated human-only and AI-only phases.

sources.title: The AI Memory Gap: Users Misremember What They Created With AI or Without

tracks.name: Synthetic Consensus Illusion
tracks.idea: Many generated answers can look like independent agreement even when they inherit the same sources, training patterns or retrieval result.
tracks.testablePrediction: People should rate a claim as better supported when it appears in several differently worded AI answers, even when all answers are explicitly derived from one original source; source-lineage disclosure should reduce the effect.

tracks.name: Confidence Transfer
tracks.idea: Confident model language may transfer confidence to a human decision even when the underlying evidence is weak.
tracks.testablePrediction: For the same answer quality, high-certainty AI wording should increase user confidence and reliance more than calibrated wording; showing objective model accuracy should moderate the effect.

sources.title: Large Language Models are overconfident and amplify human bias
